newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- The director of China's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Lu Ping, said the Preparatory Committee had completed its mission and should be disbanded. The election of the first legislature of the Special Administrative Region, as Hong Kong will be known after China takes over on July 1, should be handled by the post-handover government, he said.

-- SING TAO -- To strengthen control over the media before the 15th general conference of the Communist Party, Beijing closed down another 300 newspapers and magazines. Instructions were also issued to publications to reduce the number of negative reports.

-- WEN WEI PO -- According to a report by the International Monetary Fund, Hong Kong has become part of the world's advanced economic system. The IMF, confident about the territory's future, anticipated closer ties between the Hong Kong and mainland economies.

-- China's Premier Li Peng said Chinese and foreign companies in Hong Kong would be treated equally after the handover, and that all commercial activities which were in line with the Basic Law, the territory's post-handover constitution, could develop smoothly.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Newly listed Beijing Enterprises, the window company of the Beijing municipal government, will be injected with good-quality assets because of its special relationship with the mainland's capital city. Beijing's vice-mayor and the chairman of Beijing Enterprises said the company would be an important channel for Beijing to attract foreign investment.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Chief Secretary Anson Chan said a credible post-handover legislature was vital to boosting local and international confidence in the territory's future.
-- A consortium headed by the Lai Sun Group and the New World Group won the lucrative rights to sell duty-free liquor and tobacco at Chek Lap Kok airport.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chen Po-sum, a former stock exchange vice-chairman at the heart of a $1.6 million bribery case, was acquitted of eight charges relating to the sale of trading floor seats.
